research: Reviewed B013 (Hobo 2.0, 2026-10-20: day, things and demo angles) and the Hobo Bag's Black Friday batch B014: no angle, hook or line repeated.

The owner's own idea for this bag: tie it to the chair (the Hobo 2.0's table strap) with real footage of that strap and a studio scene made from the real bag; Pacsafe-style 'locks the bag to furniture' is the research's concept 1 (docs/research/2026-10-black-friday-and-bag-ads.md).
Layered-security argument from the same research (Pacsafe feature pointouts, self-locking zips, RFID pocket); numbers avoided because the facts list five features, not six.

Compliance: only the packet's facts for this bag (lockable zippers, RFID lining, cut-resistant strap, table strap, hidden pockets and smart compartments, 50% off, free pouch wallet, free US shipping); no warranty / returns line (the Hobo 2.0's facts do not state them), no countdown, no 'theft-proof'.

projects.title: Tie it to the chair
projects.big_idea: A café scene about the one thing nobody solves: where the bag goes when you sit down. The Hobo 2.0's table strap loops round the chair, so the bag stays right where you left it, and the lockable zippers and cut-resistant strap back it up.
projects.why_new: B013 listed the Hobo 2.0's security features. This turns the single most visual one, the table strap, into the whole story with real footage of the strap looped round a chair and table leg, and puts the other features behind it as a layered answer.

chapters.text: You sit down for a coffee. Where does your bag go? On the floor, under the table, where it can be kicked? Hanging on the back of the chair, where you can't see it?
The Hobo 2.0 has a table strap that loops around your chair, so your bag stays right where you left it.
Loop it round the chair, sit back, and enjoy your coffee. The bag is right there, close to you, and it isn't going anywhere. Do the same at the next table, and the one after.
The zippers lock, too, so nobody can open it in a crowd. One lock on each zip, and the bag stays closed while you talk.
The strap itself is cut-resistant, so a quick snip on a busy street is not an option.
Inside, an RFID lining that blocks card scanners, plus hidden pockets and smart compartments for everything else. Cards in one spot, phone in another, keys at hand.
And you get a free pouch wallet to go with it, for the little things you want close.
It's Black Friday. Fifty percent off the Hobo 2.0, with a free pouch wallet and free US shipping. Tap the link below.

projects.title: Security, layer by layer
projects.big_idea: A bag is only as safe as its weakest spot, so the Hobo 2.0 is built in layers: the zippers lock, the strap resists cuts, the table strap anchors it to a chair, the lining blocks card scanners, the pockets stay hidden. One layer per beat, each shown in use.
projects.why_new: A layered argument (each beat adds one more thing a thief would have to get past) instead of a list or a day: the structure is a build-up, and the picture changes with every layer (zip, strap, chair, lining, pocket).

chapters.text: So the Hobo 2.0 is built in layers. Every layer is one more thing to get past, and none of them gets in your way.
First, the zippers. They lock, so nobody can open the bag in a crowd. Close it, lock it, and walk on.
Next, the strap. It's cut-resistant, so it stays on your shoulder even when the street is busy.
Then the table strap. It loops around your chair, so your bag stays right where you left it, even when you look away.
Inside, an RFID lining that blocks card scanners. Your cards stay yours.
And hidden pockets and smart compartments keep the little things out of sight and in order. Cards, keys, lipstick, each in its own place.
That's the idea: not one big promise, but lots of small ones stacked up, so the bag does the worrying for you.
